`minds-admin cutover migrate` now carries a workspace's machine-owned latchkey state onto the gen-2 VM. The harvest reads, off the live gen-1 VM, the machine-owned files under the VM root's `~/.latchkey` (the credential store, `config.json`, `permissions.json`, the format stamp, the container tunnel key pair, `gateway_run.sh`, the bundled extension; the logs and the desktop-mirrored files stay behind), both supervisord drop-ins and the four tmpfs gateway secrets, base64 so they round-trip byte for byte; they are kept 0600 under the state dir's `keys/<host_db_id>/latchkey/` (mirroring their VM paths) and shredded with the SSH keys once the workspace is re-leased. The restore installs the pinned latchkey software on the new VM (the same installer the desktop provisions with), replays the files and drop-ins before the container is recreated, and, once the container is up, writes the tmpfs secrets (after the RAM-backed filesystem check) and starts `latchkey-gateway` and `latchkey-tunnel`, so a migrated workspace's service sign-ins and gateway come back without waiting for the user's desktop. Before the 2026-09-13 staging drill found this, both migrated workspaces came back signed out of every service.

An origin with no `~/.latchkey` skips the latchkey leg; an origin whose gateway was down (disk files but no tmpfs pair) gets the software and files but no start, and the desktop's next provisioning pass supplies the pair. The plan (`ABSENT` / `DISK_ONLY` / `FULL`) is recorded on the workspace's state record so a resumed run knows it without re-reading the origin; records written before this change keep working (nothing was harvested, so nothing replays). The harvest refuses before the stop when the origin's tunnel drop-in dials a port the container does not publish (or names no port, or the container publishes no sshd port), or when the origin holds the gateway's tmpfs pair without the wrapper and drop-ins a replay would restart, and the health probe additionally requires both VM latchkey programs `RUNNING` and the gateway bound on its loopback port when the gateway was replayed. The migrate report's per-workspace detail names what was carried.

The README's command list names the cutover group's real subcommands (`preflight`, `migrate`, `rollback`, `repave`) and what each does; it previously listed `drain` and `restore`, which do not exist.

Workspace stop kinds (`specs/workspace-stop-kinds.md`): `minds-admin workspaces stop` requires `--kind maintenance|idle|suspension`, and the new `workspaces set-stop-kind` changes a stopped workspace's kind (`idle` hands a held workspace back to its owner without a rollback, as long as the migrate has not parked it: a parked row stays refused by the connector's parked-row guard and needs `cutover rollback`). `server drain` stops workspaces as `idle` (their owners' next start restores them), and `cutover migrate` stops them as `maintenance`, so from the stop request to the finish CAS the owner's start is refused and no desktop's unattended recovery starts the workspace -- the race that failed the 2026-09-13 staging re-test. The migrate probes the connector for stop kinds before any stop (up front when a candidate is running, and again right before each product stop) and refuses on a connector without migration 042; its finish CAS clears the kind, the rollback's park stamps `maintenance`, and the row poll runs every 5 seconds instead of 15.
